aliases.text: Prone Scapular Retraction - Arms at Side

setup: Lie face down on a mat with your forehead resting on a small rolled towel to keep the neck in a neutral alignment.
Extend your arms straight out to the sides perpendicular to your torso in a 'T' position, palms facing downward or thumbs pointing toward the ceiling.
steps: Initiate the movement by drawing your shoulder blades toward each other across your upper back.
Lift your arms a few inches off the floor through the scapular retraction rather than forcing the movement from the lower back.
Hold the fully retracted position for the prescribed duration (typically 2 to 3 seconds), feeling a firm squeeze between the shoulder blades.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position under control.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pinch your shoulder blades together and lift your arms; inhale as you lower them back to the floor.
cues: Pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Keep your neck relaxed and forehead down
Lead with the scaps, not just the hands

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders upward toward the ears using the upper trapezius.
common_faults.correction: Keep the shoulders depressed away from your ears throughout the movement.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the neck or lifting the chest off the floor to compensate.
common_faults.correction: Keep your forehead gently resting on the towel and isolate movement to the shoulder blades.

precautions: Stop if you experience sharp anterior shoulder pain or neck strain.

name: Prone Scapular Retraction

summary: A postural rehabilitation exercise performed lying face down to strengthen the middle trapezius and rhomboids through targeted shoulder blade retraction.
